blocks.content: Every winter, cities across North India disappear under a thick layer of smog. People blame traffic. Industries. Weather. But one silent contributor continues to dominate headlines — stubble burning, locally known as parali jalana.

As a student living in Delhi, Ayush Paul did not just observe the problem. He decided to solve it. This is the story of how a school student transformed concern into innovation and carried a farmer-focused environmental solution from a classroom idea to a National Level Science Exhibition.
The Problem — Why Stubble Burning Is One of India’s Biggest Environmental Challenges

After harvesting crops like rice and wheat, farmers face a difficult challenge. They must quickly clear leftover crop residue to prepare fields for the next cultivation cycle. Farmers usually have two options: Manually remove stubble — expensive and time-consuming, or Burn the residue — fast but environmentally destructive.
Because time and cost pressures are real, burning becomes the practical choice.

For Ayush, this was not just a science topic. It was personal. Watching senior citizens struggle with polluted air, schools closing due to smog, and daily news discussions about parali burning made him ask one powerful question: “Instead of blaming farmers, can science help them?”
National Selection — 52nd Rashtriya Bal Vaigyanik Pradarshani (RBVP) 2025
Official communication from the Department of Education in Science and Mathematics confirmed participation in: 52nd Rashtriya Bal Vaigyanik Pradarshani (RBVP) 2025 at RIE Bhopal.
Technical Explanation — How the Stubble Solution Works

• Ammonium Sulfate — promotes microbial growth
  • Magnesium Sulfate — activates decomposition enzymes
  • Phosphoric Acid — breaks lignin structures
  • Humic Acid — improves soil fertility
During burning, specially designed tablets reduce emissions by capturing acidic gases and improving combustion efficiency. Estimated Impact: Up to 90% reduction in harmful pollutants.
